Murloc's Felfired Food is a limited-time promotional pop-up event created by Blizzard Entertainment in collaboration with Chain, held in Silverlake, Los Angeles, through 17-19 October 2025. The event was designed to celebrate the launch of Legion Remix, a time-limited game mode that revisits the expansion with accelerated progression, phased content updates, and expanded rewards. The pop-up featured a themed fast-casual menu inspired by the fictional taverns of Azeroth, reinterpreting classic American through the lens of fantasy universe. Tickets were priced at $50 per person and included a full meal, themed cocktails, and collectible merchandise. Attendance was limited to guests on Chain's

Mylton Fyreswyd is an Arathi located in Empire's Edge Tavern in Mereldar in Hallowfall. When Beledar shifted, Mylton was caught out on the coast and would have been a meal for the kobyss if Faerin hadn't been on patrol. When Hallowfall once again came under threat by the Sureki and the army was stretched thin, a call to arms was issued to those with the strength to wield a weapon. Mylton answered the call, joining the Flame's Radiance. He was stationed at Lothar's Landing.

An affix changes how mobs behave in a Mythic+ dungeon run. Affixes appear on all Mythic+ dungeon keys, but the number and type depend on the keystone level. The first affix is gained at level 2, the second at level 5, and the third at level 10. If the Keystone has an affix listed on it, then all of the enemies in that Mythic+ dungeon will inherit this property unless specified. Active affixes are set game-wide on a week-by-week basis and remain the same for all players until the next weekly reset. This means that every keystone will have the same set of level 2, 5, and 14 affixes for the week. Information about each affix appears on the Font of Power interface, the Mythic+ Dungeons interface

.]] Mythic+ Dungeons provides a weekly summary of all the characters on the same account that have done a Mythic+ for the week. It can be accessed from the Group Finder. Entering a Mythic dungeon will have a Font of Power at the beginning of the dungeon, the tool used to insert a Mythic Keystone (item) to start a Mythic+ difficulty.

Nameplates are floating frames anchored to units that display key information. They appear above players and NPCs, providing health, casting, and limited aura information. Nameplates allow players to monitor multiple units without relying solely on the target or focus frames. will enhance the default nameplate system by improving how important combat information is surfaced without relying on addons. Nameplates can now display a wider range of relevant buffs and debuffs, highlight dangerous or encounter‑critical casts with more prominent visuals, and present crowd‑control effects more clearly in PvP. Nashabor (meaning "Settlement of Blades" in Draenei) is a planet in the Great Dark Beyond where the Nethersent have found refuge. Tul'amar, Twice-Exiled describes it as a world of natural beauty, where crimson salt plains give way to cool, purple lakes, while the rivers are choked with huge, sturdy lillypads. The young Nethersent here learn to fight early, far earlier than they did on Argus, as martial and arcane skill is essential to survive attacks from its great, intelligent beasts. At some point, the naaru T'era found her way to Nashabor, however, there was disagreement among the Nethersent on whether or not she should be welcome. Nerubian sages, also known as viziers or nerubian priests, are a type of tall and highly intelligent nerubians. In Azjol-Nerub, they served as advisors, sorcerers, and seers to the spiderlords prior to the War of the Spider. In Azj-Kahet, they commonly appear as alchemists and battlefield spellcasters. Being derived from the aqir sages, nerubian sages were alchemically re-introduced to serve as spell-casters, wielders of the powers of the Old Gods, and keepers of genetic memory (similar to queens).

Hulks are a monstrously huge bipedal form of nerubian, built like a C'Thrax. They were created during the refining of the ascension process, with many of these monstrous creatures being used as guardians and watchdogs by the Sureki forces within Nerub-ar Palace. Created by Ansurek's evolutionary experimentation, they are guardians of her throne. The monstrous Ulgrax the Devourer stands as the first line of defense against would-be invaders of the palace. Many of these creations are crazed and those that fail to ascend properly are turned into them. They are kept deep under the City of Threads within a hidden delve known as The Underkeep. A non-player character (or NPC) is any character a player can encounter and interact with in World of Warcraft that is not controlled by another human — they are generated and controlled by the game server. NPCs are either Neutral or affiliated with a particular faction ( Alliance or Horde). Characters cannot attack NPCs of their own faction, and must be "at war" (as set in the Reputation tab of the character sheet) with a neutral NPC's faction in order to attack them. The Oasis is the primary eco-dome located on K'aresh, at the northern end of the eastern island. Within this, Project Eco-Dome is carried out by Ve'nari and Cartel Om with the backing of the K'aresh Trust. Most of the Ecological Succession storyline plays out here. The area dynamically changes based on how far along the player is in the Ecological Succession campaign, adding more activities for the world quest version as well as new characters and animals that inhabit the area.
